topic_ko: 감정 먼저, 이성은 나중 — 뇌의 자동 위험 감지기
_note: 유형별 묶음 구조. 같은 40번 지문이라도 유형마다 passage를 다르게 paraphrase 한다. order/insert/irrelevant/writing 은 구조상 예외. grammar/vocab 은 틀린 형태를 본문에 실제로 넣어 정답으로 표기.

passage: Every day we step into the world and quickly judge what is safe and what is appropriate.
According to psychologist Joseph LeDoux, an unconscious "danger detector" decides whether something or someone is safe before our conscious mind even gets started.
If that detector labels an object or person as dangerous, the so-called "fight or flight" fear response is triggered at once.
We may correct the detector's mistakes when we consciously notice them, but more often we simply invent reasons for why it was right all along.
Although we are sure our choices are purely rational, most of our decisions are actually made by emotion first, and only afterward do we gather facts to justify them.
By the time something merely "feels" dangerous, we have already begun to act inside before any real thinking has taken place.
choices: how people gradually learn to think more rationally as they grow older
how the fight-or-flight response damages our long-term health
why some people are naturally braver in dangerous situations than others
why the brain decides emotionally first and then builds reasons to support it
how we can train ourselves to remove emotion from every decision
theme.explanation_ko: 위험 평가는 의식 전에 자동·감정적으로 일어나며, 우리는 그렇게 내린 결정을 나중에 사실로 뒷받침한다는 글. '감정으로 먼저 결정하고 그 뒤 이유를 만든다'가 주제이다. ④가 정답.
theme.distractor_ko: ①나이에 따른 합리성 학습, ②투쟁-도피의 건강 피해, ③사람마다 다른 용기, ⑤감정 제거 훈련은 본문 초점이 아니다.

passage: We like to believe that our everyday judgments about safety are calm and reasonable.
Yet the psychologist Joseph LeDoux argues that an unconscious "danger detector" rates safety before we can consciously decide anything.
Once it senses a threat, a "fight or flight" reaction fires before thought begins.
We rarely overturn that first impression; instead we busily produce reasons for why it must have been correct.
In truth, most human decisions are made emotionally first, and the facts are collected afterward only to justify them.
So we should admit that emotion, not pure logic, usually leads, and treat our own reasoning with humble caution.
choices: 우리의 결정은 대개 감정이 먼저 이끄므로 자신의 이성을 겸손히 의심해야 한다.
위험한 상황에서는 본능보다 논리를 우선시해야 한다.
감정은 의사결정에서 가능한 한 완전히 배제해야 한다.
공포 반응은 훈련을 통해 충분히 없앨 수 있다.
전문가의 판단을 자신의 직관보다 항상 신뢰해야 한다.
claim.explanation_ko: 대부분의 결정이 감정으로 먼저 내려지고 이성은 그것을 정당화할 뿐이므로, 자신의 '이성적' 판단을 겸손히 의심해야 한다는 주장. ①이 정답.
claim.distractor_ko: ②논리 우선, ③감정 배제, ④공포 반응 제거, ⑤전문가 신뢰는 본문의 핵심 주장과 무관하거나 지엽적이다.

passage: Each day we make countless snap judgments about what is safe and proper.
Joseph LeDoux suggests these begin with an unconscious "danger detector" that rates safety before conscious thought starts.
When it flags danger, the "fight or flight" response occurs immediately.
Although we may fix its errors when we notice them, we usually just generate reasons to defend its first verdict.
Most human decisions, in fact, are made emotionally first, after which we gather facts to justify them.
Thus, long before we "think," we have already reacted within.
choices: 공포 반응은 인간의 생존에 거의 도움이 되지 않는다.
충분히 분석하면 인간은 언제나 합리적 결정을 내릴 수 있다.
안전에 대한 판단은 사람마다 완전히 다르다.
우리는 의식 전에 감정으로 위험을 자동 판단하고, 결정은 나중에 사실로 정당화한다.
gist.explanation_ko: 의식하기 전에 감정으로 위험을 자동 판단하고, 그 감정적 결정을 뒤에 사실로 정당화한다는 것이 요지. ⑤가 정답.
gist.distractor_ko: ①공포 반응 무용론, ②완전한 합리성, ③이론의 적용 어려움, ④개인차는 요지가 아니다.

passage: Before we consciously weigh anything, an unconscious "danger detector" has already judged whether it is safe.
This is what psychologist Joseph LeDoux proposed about how the mind responds to threat.
When it senses danger, the "fight or flight" reaction fires in an instant.
We seldom revise that snap verdict; more often we manufacture reasons to confirm it.
Indeed, most decisions are made emotionally first, and only later do we collect facts to back them up.
Feeling, it turns out, runs ahead of thought.
choices: How to Train Your Brain to Be Perfectly Logical
Feeling First, Reasoning Later: The Mind's Automatic Danger Detector
The Hidden Dangers of the Fight-or-Flight Response
Why Experts Make Better Decisions Than We Do
Calm Thinking: The Secret to a Stress-Free Life
title.explanation_ko: 의식 전 자동 위험 감지로 감정이 먼저 결정하고 이성은 뒤따른다는 핵심을 압축한 ②가 제목.
title.distractor_ko: ①완전한 논리 훈련, ③투쟁-도피의 위험, ④전문가의 결정, ⑤스트레스 없는 삶은 초점이 아니다.

passage: Every day we make rapid calls about what is safe and what is not.
Joseph LeDoux suggests an unconscious "danger detector" rates safety before conscious thought can begin.
When it senses danger, a "fight or flight" response occurs at once.
We rarely correct it; instead we generate reasons for why it was accurate in the first place.
Most decisions, in reality, are made emotionally, after which we collect facts to justify them.
In other words, we have already launched into action internally before we have even started "thinking."
implication.underlined: we have already launched into action internally before we have even started
choices: physical exercise prepares the body to face real danger
people who think slowly are usually safer than others
our emotional reaction comes before, and shapes, our conscious thinking
conscious planning always improves the quality of our choices
we should never trust any feeling without solid evidence
implication.explanation_ko: '생각을 시작하기도 전에 이미 내부적으로 행동에 돌입해 있다'는 곧 감정적 반응이 의식적 사고보다 먼저 일어나 사고를 좌우한다는 뜻이다. ③이 정답.
implication.distractor_ko: ①신체 운동, ②느린 사고의 안전, ④의식적 계획의 우월성, ⑤증거 없는 감정 불신은 밑줄의 의미와 다르다.

passage: Every day we go out into the world and make decisions about what is safe or not.
Joseph LeDoux has suggested that an unconscious "danger detector" determines what something is safe before we consciously decide.
When an object or person is assessed to be dangerous, a fear response called "fight or flight" occurs.
We may correct a mistake in this detector when we notice it, but often we simply begin generating reasons for why it was accurate.
We are generally convinced that our decisions are rational, but in reality most of them are made emotionally, and then we collect facts to justify them.
grammar.explanation_ko: ② '안전한지 아닌지'를 판단한다는 의미이므로 명사절을 이끄는 접속사는 'what' 이 아니라 'whether(~인지 아닌지)' 가 와야 한다. 'something is safe' 는 빠진 성분이 없는 완전한 절이라 의문대명사 what 은 올 수 없다('determines whether something is safe'). ②가 정답.
grammar.distractor_ko: ①about의 목적어로 쓰인 간접의문문 what is safe or not, ③a fear response를 수식하는 과거분사 called, ④begin의 목적어인 동명사 generating, ⑤동사 are made를 수식하는 부사 emotionally는 모두 옳다.

passage: Every day we make quick decisions about what is safe or not and what is appropriate or not.
Joseph LeDoux suggests an unconscious "danger detector" judges safety before we consciously decide.
When something is assessed to be dangerous, a fear response known as "fight or flight" occurs.
We may correct this detector's mistake when we notice it, but often we just generate reasons for why it was wrong.
We believe our decisions are rational, yet in reality most are made emotionally, and then we collect facts to justify these decisions.
vocab.explanation_ko: ④ 우리는 감지기의 첫 판단을 고치기보다 그것이 '정확했다(accurate)'는 이유를 만들어 낸다는 문맥이다. '틀렸다(wrong)'는 정반대 의미라 부적절하므로 accurate로 고쳐야 한다. ④가 정답.
vocab.distractor_ko: ①appropriate(적절한), ②unconscious(무의식적인), ③dangerous(위험한), ⑤justify(정당화하다)는 모두 문맥에 적절하다.

passage: We constantly judge what is safe before we are even aware of doing so.
Joseph LeDoux calls this an unconscious "danger detector" that rates safety before conscious thought begins.
When it senses danger, the "fight or flight" response fires immediately.
We seldom overturn its verdict; instead we generate reasons to confirm it was right.
In reality, most human decisions are made __________, and the facts are gathered only afterward to justify them.
Long before we "think," we have already reacted within.
blank.explanation_ko: 위험 감지기가 의식 전에 작동하고 사실은 '나중에' 모은다는 흐름이므로, 결정은 '감정으로 먼저(emotionally first)' 내려진다. ④가 정답.
blank.distractor_ko: ①신중한 분석, ②전문가 추종, ③오랜 사고 후, ⑤감정 없이는 '감정이 먼저'라는 흐름과 반대이거나 어긋난다.

irrelevant.intro: Every day we judge what is safe long before our conscious mind has time to weigh the evidence.
sentences: Joseph LeDoux suggests an unconscious "danger detector" rates safety before conscious thought can even begin.
When this detector senses a threat, the "fight or flight" fear response is triggered almost instantly.
Regular aerobic exercise has been shown to strengthen the heart and lower blood pressure over time.
We rarely correct the detector; instead we generate reasons for why its first verdict was accurate.
Thus most decisions are made emotionally first, and we only gather supporting facts afterward.
irrelevant.explanation_ko: 글은 '의식 전 자동 위험 감지와 감정 우선 결정'을 다루는데, ③ '유산소 운동이 심장을 튼튼히 하고 혈압을 낮춘다'는 무관한 내용이다.
irrelevant.distractor_ko: ①②④⑤는 모두 무의식적 위험 감지와 감정적 결정의 정당화라는 주제로 연결된다.

order.given: Every day we make decisions about what is safe and what is not, often without realizing how the process begins.

blocks.A: What starts it is what Joseph LeDoux calls an unconscious "danger detector," which rates safety before we can consciously decide; when it senses a threat, the "fight or flight" response fires at once.
blocks.B: We may correct this detector when we consciously notice its error, but more often we simply generate reasons for why it was accurate in the first place.
blocks.C: In the end, then, most decisions are made emotionally first, and only afterward do we collect the facts that justify them.

order.explanation_ko: 주어진 글의 '판단이 어떻게 시작되는가'를 (A)가 '위험 감지기'로 설명, (B)가 그 감지기를 우리가 어떻게 다루는지(고치기보다 정당화)를 잇고, (C)가 'In the end'로 결론을 요약. (A)-(B)-(C).
order.distractor_ko: (C)의 In the end는 결론이라 첫 순서가 될 수 없고, (B)의 'this detector'는 (A)에서 감지기가 소개된 뒤라야 가리킬 대상이 생긴다.

insert.insert_sentence: When it senses a threat, the "fight or flight" fear response fires almost instantly.

passage_marked.text: Every day we make rapid judgments about what is safe and what is not.
Joseph LeDoux suggests an unconscious "danger detector" rates safety before conscious thought can begin.
We rarely correct this detector; instead we generate reasons for why it was right in the first place.
Thus most decisions are made emotionally first, and we collect supporting facts only afterward.
Long before we "think," we have already reacted within.

insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장의 'it'은 위험 감지기를 가리키며 '위협을 감지하면 공포 반응이 일어난다'는 내용이므로, 감지기를 소개한 문장(②) 바로 뒤에 와야 한다. ②가 정답.
insert.distractor_ko: 감지기가 소개되기 전(①)에는 'it'이 가리킬 대상이 없고, 그 뒤 문장들은 이미 감지기의 작동을 전제로 이어진다.

passage: Joseph LeDoux argues that an unconscious "danger detector" judges safety before our conscious mind even starts.
When it flags a threat, the "fight or flight" response fires at once.
We seldom revise that snap verdict; instead we generate reasons for why it was right.
In reality, most human decisions are made emotionally first.
Only afterward do we collect or invent the facts that justify those decisions.
So feeling runs ahead of thought, and reasoning mostly follows to defend what we have already chosen.
summary.summary_template: We assess danger in an __(A)__ way before conscious thought, and then we gather facts to __(B)__ the decisions we have already made emotionally.
summary.explanation_ko: 위험 평가는 의식 전에 일어나는 (A)automatic(자동적인) 과정이고, 우리는 감정으로 먼저 내린 결정을 (B)support(뒷받침)할 사실을 모은다. ③.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)는 automatic, (B)는 support여야 한다. deliberate/rational/slow(자동성과 반대), reject/weaken/question(정당화와 반대)은 글과 어긋난다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.answer: Most human decisions are made emotionally.
writing.explanation_ko: 주어 Most human decisions + 수동태 are made + 부사 emotionally('감정적으로 내려진다').

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 우리는 이 결정을 정당화하기 위해 사실을 수집한다.
writing.answer: We collect the facts to justify these decisions.
writing.explanation_ko: 주어 We + 동사 collect + 목적어 the facts + 목적의 to부정사 to justify these decisions.

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 어떤 것이 위험하다고 평가되면, 공포 반응이 일어난다.
writing.answer: When something is assessed to be dangerous, a fear response occurs.
writing.explanation_ko: When + 주어 something + 수동태 is assessed to be dangerous, 주절 a fear response occurs.

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 흐름상 빈칸에 들어갈 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.context: We are generally convinced that our decisions are "rational," but most of them are actually made ___________.
writing.explanation_ko: '이성적(rational)'이라는 믿음과 대비되는, 결정이 실제로 내려지는 방식은 '감정적으로(emotionally)'이다.

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: An unconscious "danger detector" determines whether something is safe before we can even begin to consciously make a determination.
writing.answer: 무의식적인 '위험 감지기'가, 우리가 의식적으로 판단을 내리기 시작하기도 전에, 어떤 것이 안전한지 아닌지를 결정한다.
writing.explanation_ko: whether ~(인지 아닌지) 명사절, before we can even begin to ~(우리가 ~하기 시작하기도 전에).

writing.question: 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 본문에 근거하여 쓰시오.
writing.summary: We judge danger in an (A)___________ way before conscious thought, and then collect facts to (B)___________ decisions we have already made emotionally.
writing.explanation_ko: (A) 위험 평가는 의식 전에 일어나는 자동적(automatic) 과정, (B) 감정으로 먼저 내린 결정을 뒷받침(support)할 사실을 모은다.
